whatChanged: NEW: Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint agrees to buy Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3bn, a 52% premium to the pre-rumor price; closing expected 1H 2027 (vrns-proofpoint-acquisition)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsors, strategics and insiders keep taking listed businesses off public markets. Two more signed on 15 October: Penske Corporation and Mitsui, which already control the company, will pay $212 a share for the Penske Automotive float at about $16.3bn EV (pag-penske-mitsui-take-private), and a GTCR-led consortium with activist Elliott will pay $7.75 a share, about $6.1bn EV, for CCC Intelligent Solutions (cccs-gtcr-elliott-take-private). Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint agreed on 15 October to pay $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3bn, for Varonis (vrns-proofpoint-acquisition). Ithaca Holdings is taking Bumble private at $6.05 a share (bmbl-ithaca-take-private), CD&R and McKesson are paying $32.05 a share for Option Care Health (opch-cdr-mckesson-take-private), and Viatris is tendering $36.50 a share for Pacira (pcrx-viatris-acquisition). Tender mechanics decide timing: Copart closed its ACV tender offer on 16 October with 68.4% of shares tendered (cprt-acv-acquisition), while Curaleaf's hostile Aurora bid runs to 4 December (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals keep being decided by regulators, politicians and courts rather than the parties. Paramount's ~$110bn Warner Bros. Discovery takeover closed only after a 12-state antitrust settlement (psky-wbd-acquisition). Kimberly-Clark won EU clearance for Kenvue only by agreeing to sell its EEA feminine-care brands, with China still pending (kmb-kenvue-acquisition). AkzoNobel and Axalta are expected to offer a refinish divestment for EU clearance (akza-axalta-merger). BT's rescue of TalkTalk waits on a CMA report due 19 October and a ministerial public-interest decision (bt-talktalk-acquisition). The ECB has now cleared UniCredit to control Commerzbank, but the German government's opposition remains (cbk-unicredit-takeover). Clean exits show the contrast: Brazil's CADE cleared Transocean-Valaris without conditions (val-transocean-acquisition).

themes.label: Large-caps scaling up buybacks on surplus cash
themes.note: Companies with cash coming in faster than they can reinvest it keep expanding share repurchases, each tying the bigger programme to a specific cash or capital tailwind. Nvidia added $150bn to its authorization on AI-accelerator cash flow (nvda-buyback-2026). TotalEnergies lifted Q4 buybacks to $2.5bn and pledged more than 5% annual dividend growth as oil trades around $100 (tte-buyback-dividend-2026). Canadian banks are moving together: TD has OSFI approval and began buying back up to another C$10bn on 9 October (td-buyback-2026), and Scotiabank lifted its issuer bid to 40 million shares (bns-buyback-2026). Julius Baer announced a CHF600m buyback days after FINMA closed its Signa probe (baer-buyback-2026).

themes.label: European incumbents consolidating domestic rivals for scale
themes.note: Europe's large banks and industrials are bidding for rivals to get the scale to compete with US and Chinese peers, with controlling shareholders, governments and supervisors deciding outcomes. The ECB has cleared UniCredit to move past 30% of Commerzbank with no cap, putting control within reach around year-end despite Berlin's opposition (cbk-unicredit-takeover). Intesa Sanpaolo has sweetened its Monte dei Paschi offer and won Delfin's backing, but the MPS board still calls it too low (isp-bmps-takeover-offer). Evonik rejected BASF's approach, leaving RAG-Stiftung's ~43% stake decisive (evk-basf-acquisition). KKR and RWE (un01-rwe-kkr-acquisition) and Apollo (un01-apollo-acquisition) are bidding for Uniper, and RHI Magnesita faces a 27 October put-up-or-shut-up deadline for Vesuvius (vsvs-rhim-takeover-proposal).

themes.label: Governments selling state-held stakes to strategic and financial buyers
themes.note: Several governments are privatising long-held stakes and choosing buyers on price plus industrial plan. India's cabinet approved selling 60.72% of IDBI Bank (government and LIC) to Fairfax for ₹52,878 crore, keeping 34% between them (ffh-idbi-bank-acquisition). Portugal picked Lufthansa's all-cash offer for 44.9% of TAP Air Portugal over Air France-KLM while keeping a 50.1% majority (lha-tap-stake-acquisition). Germany is selling up to 74.12% of Uniper to meet EU rules, drawing a KKR-RWE joint bid (un01-rwe-kkr-acquisition) and a separate Apollo bid (un01-apollo-acquisition).
